title: Placing the Notes
summary: Places the twelve notes: the open end and a mark 4/10 down from the mouth-hole sound an octave apart, and each other note goes midway, or at equal divisions, between notes already set. Also: enlarging flat holes, shrinking sharp ones, moving holes for the fingers, hole sizes as fractions of the circumference, tuning by ear.

prev.title: The Kinds of Flute and Suitable Materials

blocks.text: Placing the Notes

blocks.verse:
यत्र फूत्कार भंदेन क्रमात् पंचस्वरोदयः।
सस प सा ग इत्येव स वंश शास्त्र संमतः।।१६।।
blocks.text: That bamboo in which, by varying the blowing, five notes arise in order, Sa, Sa, Pa, Sa, Ga, is the one approved by the śāstra of the flute.

So if I have to make a flute, I shall need a pipe or bamboo long enough to be about ten times its antaḥparidhi (inner circumference). In it, at the first dasāṃśa (one-tenth) from one end, that is 10/1, make the hole of the mukharandhra (mouth-hole).

The roundness of the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) will be 1/3, that is one-third, of the antarvyāsa (inner diameter). From the other end too, at a distance of the first dasāṃśa (one-tenth), that is 10/1, make a hole whose inner diameter is half, that is 1/2, of the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference). So the length left from the mouth-hole to that second hole is 8 times, by the paridhimāna. And taking as Sa the nāda (sound) that arises when blowing into the mouth-hole, place the further notes in the following way -
Now, before [placing] the six notes, one must find a place where, by making a hole, a note exactly one saptaka (octave) higher, that is (Ṡa), can sound. On this there is the following śloka.

blocks.verse:
अन्तः परिधि मानेन मुख रन्ध्रा च्चतुर्गुणे।
परिमाणे षडजस्तारों यदि मध्यो दशमे स्थितः।।१७।।
blocks.text: By the measure of the inner circumference, at four times [that measure] from the mouth-hole lies the upper Ṣaḍja, if the middle [Ṣaḍja] lies at the tenth.

The meaning of the above śloka is that the length from the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) to the far end of the pipe, measured by the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference) given before, may be as much as nine times and as little as six times.

Now, whatever the length from the mouth-hole to the end, the sound that comes out when it is blown is named (madhya Sa, middle Sa). Now divide the distance from madhya Sa to the mouth-hole into ten equal parts, and at 4/10 part from the mouth-hole, that is at 6/10 part from madhya Sa, make a mark with a pencil; its name will be tāra Ṡa (upper Sa). After this, between these two Sas, 11 more marks will have to be made in the way given below; then in all 11+2=13 notes will have been placed, whose names will be: Sa, komal Re, Re, komal Ga, Ga, Ma, Ma′, Pa, komal Dha, Dha, komal Ni, Ni, Ṡa.

blocks.verse:
षडजद्वय मध्ये तु मध्यमः स्वर इष्यते।
षडज मध्यमयो र्मध्ये रिषभः स्थाप्यो मनीषिभीः।।१८।।
blocks.text: Between the two Ṣaḍjas the Madhyama note is wanted; between Ṣaḍja and Madhyama the wise should place Ṛṣabha.
That is, between the two Sas make the mark for the śuddha (natural) Madhyama note, and between that Madhyama and madhya Sa place śuddha Ṛṣabha.

Here the derivation of Ṣaḍja fits as follows: the note that ṣaṭ svarān, that is six notes, janayati, that is gives birth to, is called Ṣaḍja; and the note that stands in the middle of the saptaka (octave) is called Madhyama. In short these are called Sa and Ma, and Ṛṣabha is called Re.

blocks.verse:
रिषभमध्यमयोर्मध्ये गान्धारद्वय कल्पना।
अपरषडज् मध्यमयोर्मध्ये कोमल धैवतः।।१९।।
blocks.text: Between Ṛṣabha and Madhyama two Gāndhāras are to be devised; between the other Ṣaḍja and Madhyama, komal Dhaivata.
That is, between the Ṛṣabha and Madhyama notes make the marks for two Gāndhāras at equal distance. And between tāra Sa and the Madhyama note make the mark for komal Dhaivata.

blocks.verse:
ऋजुधैवत मध्यमयोर्मध्ये स्थाप्यौस्वरौ क्रमात्।
प्रथमो मध्यमस्तीब्रो द्वितीयः पंचमोभवेत।।२०।।
blocks.text: Between ṛju Dhaivata and Madhyama two notes are to be placed in order: the first will be tīvra Madhyama, the second Pañcama.
That is, between komal Dhaivata and Madhyama understand the places of two notes at equal distance: the first will be tīvra (sharp) Madhyama and the second the Pañcama note.

blocks.verse:
ऋजुधैवत षड्जयोर्मध्ये भागास्त्रयो मताः।
प्रथमो धैवतः शुद्धो द्वितीयौ द्वौ निषादकौ।।२१।।
blocks.text: Between ṛju Dhaivata and Ṣaḍja three parts are held: the first is śuddha Dhaivata, the second [and third] the two Niṣādas.
That is, between komal Dhaivata and tāra Ṣaḍja the wise should make three equal parts and place, in order, Dhaivata and the two Niṣādas.

blocks.verse:
ऋषभषड्जयोमध्ये कोमलो ऋषभो भवेत्।
स्वरस्थानानि चैतानि द्वादशानि प्रकल्पयेत्।।२२।।
blocks.text: Between Ṛṣabha and Ṣaḍja is komal Ṛṣabha. Thus one should devise these twelve svarasthānas (note positions).
That is, between Ṛṣabha and madhya Sa is the place of komal Ṛṣabha. In this way place all twelve notes in the form of marks.

An example is given here on the basis of the rule above. Suppose we printed the roundness of a pipe or bamboo on paper and found its roundness to be about 6 sūt [a small unit of length]. Then I measured the inner girth of that roundness, opened it out and measured it: the paper that sat inside in the shape of a round ring of 6 sūt became, after opening out, about 17 sūt long, that is 1 inch 7 sūt. Now we named this paper (antaḥparidhimāna, measure of the inner circumference), and gave it a short name too, miti (the measure). Then we cut a pipe 7 times as long as this miti and found it came to about 12 inches. When a mukharandhra (mouth-hole) was made at one end, the pipe from the mouth-hole to the end was some ten and a half inches long. Now, first of all, in order to place tāra Ṣaḍja, a mark was made at a distance of four inches two sūt down from the mouth-hole and taken as tāra Ṡa. And the far end of the pipe was taken as madhya Sa, since it is between these two Sas that we have to place the 12 notes. If the space between the two Sas were divided into 6 equal parts and Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni placed in order, the flute would certainly be out of tune. For as we go on making holes moving upward, its area keeps decreasing, and in the same proportion the distance between the notes (svarāntara, interval) also keeps decreasing. It is with this fine point in mind that the rule above had to be made the basis. So in the figure the marks will not be at equal distances from bottom to top.

But after the marks are made, the holes on those marks must be made in order. By the rule above, madhya Ṣaḍja should not be taken to be the cut end of the pipe that stands naturally open. So, measuring with the miti (the measure of the inner circumference), a hole should be made at a distance of six miti from the mouth-hole, its girth about half the girth of the pipe; and about one miti below that hole should be the far end of the pipe. If a flute 7 times the miti is to be made, make the madhya Sa hole at the distance of 7 times. And if a flute longer than 7 times is to be made, place madhya Sa at that same distance too. But do not place the remaining notes by the rule above; for that we shall give some additional rules later. The rule above is only for those flutes that are 6 or 7 times their miti long. See the figure ahead.

Here, the place where the author has taken Ṣaḍja to be is, in the view of players, the place of the Pañcama note. Still, for the convenience of beginning sādhakas (learners), the Ṣaḍja given above is accepted. If, out of habit, the first hole on the flute, which is the lowest, is taken to be Pañcama rather than Ṣaḍja, then for them another method of placing the notes is set out. Although there is no special difference between this method and the one above, it is written to remove some people's doubts.

blocks.verse:
अन्तः परिधि मानेन मुखरन्ध्राच्चतुगुणे।
परिमाणे पंचमोमध्यो यदि मन्द्रो दशमे स्थितः।।२३।।
blocks.text: By the measure of the inner circumference, at four times from the mouth-hole lies the middle Pañcama, if the lower one lies at the tenth.

That is, if the other end of the pipe is at ten times from the mukharandhra (mouth-hole), then, taking that as mandra (lower) Pañcama, the Pañcama of the madhya saptaka (middle octave) must be taken at four times the distance from the mouth-hole. That is, if Pañcama is ten inches from the mouth-hole, place the second Pañcama four inches from the mouth-hole. Here it is not necessary that the length of the pipe be exactly ten times the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference). The length of the pipe can also be 7 or 8 times the paridhimāna; but we have to place madhya Pañcama by dividing that length into five equal parts and taking 2/5, or into ten parts and taking 4/10, because the remaining notes have to be placed taking just these two Pañcamas as pillars. If the far end of the pipe is not natural but artificial, that is if a hole is made and taken as the end, then in this case madhya Pañcama can be placed not at 4/10 but at 5/12. See the figure.

blocks.verse:
पंचमद्वय मध्ये तु षडजस्य स्थिति र्भवेत।
मन्द्र पंचम षडजयो र्मध्ये धैवत इष्यते।।२४।।
blocks.text: Between the two Pañcamas lies Ṣaḍja; between lower Pañcama and Ṣaḍja, Dhaivata is wanted.

That is, Ṣaḍja lies in the middle between the lower Pañcama and the upper Pañcama, and Dhaivata belongs midway between the lower Pañcama and Ṣaḍja. Here some inquirers may ask: since the distance from Dhaivata to Pañcama, counting komal Dhaivata, is two svarāntaras (intervals), and the distance from Dhaivata to Ṣaḍja, because of the two Niṣādas in between, is three intervals, why then has Dhaivata been placed midway between Ṣaḍja and Pañcama? This doubt is resolved as follows: once the hole of the Dhaivata note is made, the length of the pipe is reduced, and the result of this shortening is that within the same distance in which two notes lie below Dha, three notes can be placed above. Here a spiritual thought too will hold good: if a poor man loses ten paise and a rich man loses 10 rupees, both will feel equal distress. In the same way, in the pipe too the successive limits are seen to grow smaller: though to the ear the intervals between notes are equal, to the eye, as on a stringed instrument, the distance appears to shrink. On this basis, further on, four notes are placed within this same distance.

blocks.verse:
मन्द्र पंचम धैवतयो र्मध्ये कोमल धैवतः।
षड्ज धैवतयो र्मध्ये निषादौ द्वौ समानकौ।।२५।।
blocks.text: Between lower Pañcama and Dhaivata is komal Dhaivata; between Ṣaḍja and Dhaivata are the two Niṣādas, equally spaced.

That is, komal Dhaivata will be between the lower Pañcama and śuddha Dhaivata, and both Niṣādas will lie at equal distances between śuddha Dhaivata and Ṣaḍja. Here some may doubt: when, by the earlier rule, the gaps between the holes also contract as the pipe gets shorter, how is it that equal distances have been written for Dha, Ni, Ni and Sa? This will be resolved by the following śloka.

blocks.verse:
यदा छिद्रस्य संकोचः स्थात्तदा नादनीचता।
यदा छिद्रस्य विस्तारस्तदा स्याद् विपरीतता।।२६।।
blocks.text: When a hole is narrowed, the sound becomes lower; when a hole is widened, the reverse.

That is, in the distances between the holes of Dha, Ni, Ni and Sa there is so fine an unevenness that it is hard to solve by gaṇita (calculation). So the fault can be removed simply by making the komal Ni hole slightly smaller than the Dha hole. The proof of this can only be the attentive ear of musicians. So the meaning of the above śloka is: if the hole is narrowed, the sound becomes lower than its place, and if the hole is made bigger, the sound becomes higher than its place, that is its śruti. But this raising and lowering of the sound will be limited to four śrutis at most. Taking advantage of this procedure, we can also gain ease in the rakhāv (placement) of the fingers.

blocks.verse:
स्वस्थानाच्च्युतछिद्रस्य वृद्दधया शुद्धि र्विधीयते।
स्वस्थानोद्गत छिद्रस्य लाघवात् परिशोधनम्।।२७।।
blocks.text: A hole that has slipped from its proper place is corrected by enlarging it; a hole that has risen from its proper place, by pariśodhana (correction) through making it smaller.

That is, holes that have fallen from their proper place are corrected by making them bigger, and holes that have risen, by making them smaller. Here, the place of śuddha Dhaivata that has been fixed by calculation should in fact, by the test of the ear, be somewhat further down. But if that is done, it may be hard to place a finger on some large flute, and to find that proper place one would have to resort to laborious calculation. So to avoid these two difficulties we have raised Dhaivata a little and made it narrower, and lowered Ṣaḍja a little and made it wider, and accordingly put forward a simple form of the calculation. The further placing of the notes is as follows.

blocks.verse:
धैवतात्तु निषादस्य शुदस्य यावती मितिः।
तन्मानेन षड्जादूर्घ्वम् रिषभ इष्यते।।२८।।
blocks.text: By the measure from Dhaivata to śuddha Niṣāda, Ṛṣabha is wanted above Ṣaḍja.
That is, at whatever distance śuddha Niṣāda lies from śuddha Dhaivata, Ṛṣabha's place is at that same height above Sa.

blocks.verse:
षड्जधैवतमानेन ऋषभात्तीव्र मध्यमः।
तयोर्मध्ये च गान्धारः शुद्धस्थाप्यो मनीषिभिः।।२९।।
blocks.text: By the measure from Ṣaḍja to Dhaivata, tīvra Madhyama [is placed] from Ṛṣabha; and between the two the wise should place śuddha Gāndhāra.
Measure the distance from Sa down to Dhaivata, and place tīvra (sharp) Madhyama that same height above Ṛṣabha, and śuddha Gāndhāra in the middle between Sa and tīvra Ma′.

blocks.verse:
तीव्र मध्यम गान्धार मध्ये स्याच्छुद्ध मध्यमः।
ऋषभ षड्ज मध्ये तु कोमलो ऋषभोमतः।।३०।।
blocks.text: Between tīvra Madhyama and Gāndhāra is śuddha Madhyama; between Ṛṣabha and Ṣaḍja komal Ṛṣabha is held [to lie].
Between tīvra (sharp) Madhyama and Gāndhāra, śuddha Madhyama; and between Ṛṣabha and Ṣaḍja, komal Ṛṣabha: this is the proper placing.

blocks.verse:
रिषभ गान्धारयोर्मध्ये गान्धारः कोमलो मतः।
क्रम एषः स्वराणाम् तु द्वादशानाम् भवेदिह।।३१।।
blocks.text: Between Ṛṣabha and Gāndhāra komal Gāndhāra is held [to lie]. This is the order of the twelve notes here.

Between śuddha Ṛṣabha and Gāndhāra is the place of komal Ga. In this way the marks for the order of the 12 notes have been fixed here. Now the whole process of making is described once more in brief. First of all, measure the inner girth of the pipe or bamboo in the shape of a paper ring and open it out; the length of that bamboo should be from 9 to 10 times that. Then at one-ninth of it make the hole (surākh) of the mukharandhra (mouth-hole), its roundness one-third of the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference).

Then make a stopper of rubber, or of anything that can go inside, push it in, and bring it right up near the mouth-hole. Then blow into the mouth-hole and see whether, as the breath is increased, sounds of the kind Sa Ṡa Ṗa Ṡa come out in order. If it is right, then go on to place the notes in order by the method given above. Before placing them, take the sound that comes out by itself as mandra (lower) Pañcama; first draw a straight line, divide it into 10 parts up to the mouth-hole, and place madhya Pañcama at 4/10. Then place Sa between P̣a and Pa, Dha between Sa and P̣a, and komal Ni and Ni between Dha and Sa, and in the way described above make marks for all the notes.

blocks.verse:
अंगुली लाघवार्थ हि क्वचित् स्वस्थान लंघनम्।
हस्त लाघवमादाय छिद्राणाम् वक्रता क्वचित्।।३२।।
blocks.text: For ease of the fingers a hole sometimes leaves its proper place; and for ease of the hand the holes are sometimes set out of line.

Sometimes, when making a large flute, one also has to think whether, if the holes are made according to the marks fixed at their proper places, there will be special difficulty in placing the fingers. If there will be, some remedy is needed for that too. The above śloka gives the solution to this. First divide this difficulty into two parts: (1) the distance between the holes being greater than the spread of the fingers; (2) because the fingers are unequal, the short finger not reaching level with the long finger. Now for the first difficulty we can move the holes a little up or a little down from their fixed place; but when moving one down, do not forget to make it bigger as well, and when moving one up, to make the hole smaller than its fixed limit. In the same way, for the second difficulty we can move the holes to the right and left of the straight line. In this procedure the hole need not be made larger or smaller than its proper limit, because holes moved to the right or left of the line undergo no change in their sound. For this reason the hole of madhya Pañcama is made on the opposite side of the line, and it is closed with the thumb. Now the limits of the holes are considered: how much widening or narrowing of which hole can be justified.

blocks.verse:
अन्तः परिधिमानेन मुख रन्ध्ररूत्रयांशकः।
मानं तदेव छिद्राणाम् द्विस्वराणाम् प्रकल्पितम्।३३।
blocks.text: By the measure of the inner circumference, the mouth-hole is one-third; the same measure is set for the holes that serve two notes.

The opening of the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) will be at most a tṛtīyāṃśa (one-third) of the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference). And the sizes of the dvisvara chidras (holes serving two notes) will also be the same or a little less.

blocks.verse:
निषादद्वय कल्पे तु चतूर्थाशौ भविष्यतः।
गान्धारोभय कल्पे तु पंचमांश भविष्यतः।३४।
blocks.text: When the two Niṣādas are made [as separate holes], they will be one-fourth; when both Gāndhāras are made, they will be one-fifth.

If the Niṣādas are divided into two holes, both holes will be a quarter of the paridhimāna (measure of the circumference). If the Gāndhāras are divided into two holes, both holes will be a pañcamāṃśa (one-fifth) of the paridhimāna, 1/5.

blocks.verse:
रिध मानां च छिद्राणि द्विस्वराणि भवन्ति हि।
षड्ज पंचमयोर्मानाम् चतुर्यांश मुदाह्रतम्।३५।
blocks.text: The holes of Re, Dha and Ma are holes for two notes; the measure for Ṣaḍja and Pañcama is declared to be one-fourth.

That is, the holes made for Re, Dha and Ma should be made large, taking each as the place of two notes. Sa and Pa are acala (fixed notes), so small holes will suit them. Here by the hole of Pa is meant the last hole. Although the first hole too is the place of P̣a, this hole may also be natural. If an unnatural hole is to be made, it will have to be kept somewhat larger than the other holes.

blocks.verse:
यदि प्रलम्बो बंशः स्याछिद्रं तत्र लघुस्मृतम्।
यदि वामनवद् बंशश्छिद्रं तत्र गुरुस्मृतम्।३६।
blocks.text: If the bamboo is long, the hole there is held to be small; if the bamboo is short like a dwarf, the hole there is held to be large.
That is, if the bamboo is 10 times its paridhimāna (measure of the circumference), all the holes will be laghu (small). If it is seven times instead of ten, its holes will be large.

If this is not done, there is a chance of out-of-tuneness in Gāndhāra and Madhyama of the tāra saptaka (upper octave). In a flute where both forms of Niṣāda depend on a single hole, that hole will have to be kept somewhat larger than the Dhaivata hole. And in a flute where two holes are wanted for the two Niṣādas, both holes can be kept the same as Dhaivata's, or even a little smaller. So it is better to give all the holes a small form first, and afterwards make them bigger, matching them against a harmonium or some reliable instrument. For the solution to this fine point is audible, not visible.
